title: Banana-Oat Breakfast Buns

items.text: 4 ripe bananas, mashed (about 2 cups) — use the fresher batch, not the very old ones
½ cup high-protein vanilla soy yogurt (one 5.3 oz container, use the whole thing)
2 tablespoons grapeseed oil or softened butter

steps.text: Warm ¼ cup soy milk to 105–110°F (warm to the touch, not hot). Stir in 2 tablespoons honey, then sprinkle in 2¼ teaspoons active dry yeast. Let stand 5–10 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Creamy and visibly foamy — no need for a huge head of bubbles, just a foamy surface.

steps.text: Mash 4 ripe bananas until mostly smooth, leaving a few small pieces. Whisk in 2 eggs, the soy yogurt, ¼ cup grapeseed oil, 2 tablespoons vanilla, and the orange zest.
In a separate bowl, whisk together 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup whole-wheat flour, ½ cup oat flour, ½ teaspoon cinnamon, ¼ teaspoon nutmeg, and 1 teaspoon sea salt.
Add the bloomed yeast mixture and the banana mixture to the dry ingredients. Stir until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn onto a lightly floured surface and knead 6–8 minutes, adding flour only a tablespoon at a time if truly necessary.
steps.donenessCue: Soft, elastic, and slightly tacky — not stiff. Sticky is fine.

steps.text: Place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and let rise somewhere warm for 60–90 minutes.

While the dough rises, mix 1 cup almond flour, 2 tablespoons honey, 2 tablespoons grapeseed oil or softened butter, 1 teaspoon vanilla, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, the ½-orange zest, and ¼ teaspoon salt. Add soy milk 1 tablespoon at a time (2–3 tablespoons total) until it’s a soft, spreadable paste — not runny.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add the 2 diced old bananas and cook 2–3 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Bananas begin to soften and color.

steps.text: Add 2 tablespoons honey and cook 1–2 minutes more.
Remove from heat. Add 2 tablespoons Don Q Gold rum and a pinch of salt, then either flambé carefully or simmer 1–2 minutes to cook off the raw alcohol edge.
Let cool to room temperature before using — do not add it to the dough or filling while hot.
Turn the risen dough onto a lightly floured surface and roll into roughly a 12×18-inch rectangle.

Spread the almond-orange filling evenly over the dough, leaving about ½ inch bare around the edges. Spoon the cooled Bananas Foster mixture evenly over the top. If using, scatter ½ cup chopped pecans over everything.
Starting from the long side, roll into a fairly tight log and pinch the seam closed.
Cut into 12 equal pieces. Place each cut-side up in a lined standard 12-cup muffin tin, filling each well only about ⅔ full for now.
Cover loosely and let rise 30–45 minutes, watching the dough rather than the clock.
steps.donenessCue: Noticeably puffy, filling most of the cup.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Bake, checking starting at 18 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Tops are golden and the centers feel set, not doughy.

steps.text: Let the buns rest in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack.
Combine 3 tablespoons honey, 1 tablespoon orange juice, 1 teaspoon orange zest, ½ teaspoon vanilla, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan. Warm gently over low heat 1–2 minutes — don’t boil.
Whisk in 1 tablespoon butter, if using. Drizzle over the buns once they’ve cooled about 10 minutes.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: Scatter ½ cup chopped pecans over the filling before rolling.
Texture target: soft, pull-apart bread, not cake or dense. Banana up front, orange and cinnamon in the background, a caramelized rum-banana pocket and nutty spiral running through the center.
storage: Counter: airtight container, up to 2 days. Refrigerator: up to 5 days. Freezer: wrap individually, up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen in the microwave for 25–35 seconds, or in a 300°F oven for about 10 minutes.
